pages.summary: Tissues bring cells together for shared functions and division of labour. The page places tissues within biological organisation, compares mitosis with meiosis and plant with animal mitosis, and classifies plant tissues into meristematic and permanent groups.

text_image_disagreements.text_says: Cell Tissues Organ Organ system Organisms
text_image_disagreements.image_shows: Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms; the native arrow characters are garbled.

last_problems: [code] item i49: the unpack uses textbook Hindi for the book's own terms (पदार्थ → substance); the learner hears the book's English term in Roman, never its Hindi translation (S1-15)

p001-i3.content: TISSUE: Cells combine to perform same function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes a group of cells a tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells work together to perform a shared function; tissue refers to this functional grouping.

teacher_understanding.question: What defining criterion does the page supply?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly links cells combining with performance of the same function.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cooperation between cells useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: A multicellular body has many tasks. Specialised groups can carry out particular tasks efficiently rather than requiring each cell to do every job.

prerequisites: cell as the basic living unit
p001-i3.exam_note: Foundation for tissue identification; a random collection of cells is not the defining idea.

terms.plain_meaning: एक काम मिलकर करने वाला cells का समूह
terms.everyday_image: जैसे रसोई में एक टीम मिलकर खाना बनाती है

why_chain.step: A large body needs several jobs performed at the same time.
Cells combine for a shared function, allowing work to be distributed.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue helps move a limb.
unpack.consequence: Introduces plant and animal tissues and the need for division of labour.
unpack.visual_verb: group cells and highlight one shared task
unpack.level_extra: Some tissues contain different cell types cooperating in one broad function; identical appearance is not required.

p001-i4.content: When plant cells combine, they form plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cells constitute plant tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies plant tissues as groups formed by plant cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this category distinguished from animal tissue here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The distinction is the organismal source of its cells: plant rather than animal.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this grouping help a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different cell groups can specialise in growth, support, storage or transport within the same plant.

p001-i4.exam_note: Leads directly to the plant-tissue classification.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में मिलकर काम करने वाले cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: डंठल में पानी पहुँचाने वाली जुड़ी हुई व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Plants need growth, support and transport.
Specialised groups of plant cells perform these jobs.

unpack.example_or_place: A familiar stem contains several plant tissues.
unpack.consequence: The lower chart divides this category further.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom from a plant stem into grouped cells
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish plant tissue from an entire plant organ such as a leaf.

p001-i5.content: When animal cells combine, they form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cells form animal tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Animal cells form the tissue groups identified here.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from the previous category?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells belong to animals rather than plants, although both categories involve cells working together.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do animals need distinct tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Movement, protection and communication require different cellular specialisations, so one general-purpose group cannot perform all these jobs equally well.

terms.plain_meaning: जानवर या हमारे शरीर में मिलकर काम करने वाले cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: हाथ हिलाते समय साथ काम करते muscle cells

why_chain.step: An animal needs movement, protection and coordination.
Different tissue groups specialise in these needs.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue in the arm.
unpack.consequence: Both plants and animals show organisation through tissue formation.
unpack.visual_verb: group animal cells by job
unpack.level_extra: Humans are included within animals.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does tissue formation create division of labour?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different groups specialise in particular functions, so the body's work is distributed among them.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this different from every cell doing the same general work?
teacher_understanding.answer: A specialised group develops features suited to its task and depends on other groups for complementary tasks.

teacher_understanding.question: What consequence does the page attribute to tissue formation?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies division of labour as an outcome.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग काम अलग समूहों को बाँटना
terms.everyday_image: घर में कोई खाना बनाता है, कोई बर्तन साफ करता है

why_chain.step: Many body functions must be performed together.
Specialised tissue groups share these functions instead of each doing everything.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle produces movement while nervous tissue carries signals.
unpack.consequence: Specialisation creates cooperation and dependence between tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: distribute task cards among cell groups
unpack.level_extra: Division of labour means functional specialisation, not cell division.

p001-i7.content: Decreases workload on individual cells, hence leads to organisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does sharing functions reduce an individual cell's workload?
teacher_understanding.answer: A specialised cell need not undertake the full range of tasks required by the organism; other groups supply complementary functions.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this lead to organisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Groups with different jobs must cooperate, creating tissues and coordinated higher levels rather than a loose collection of cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What causal connection is explicitly made on the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reduced workload on individual cells is linked to organisation.

p001-i7.exam_note: Interpret workload as the range of tasks, not a claim that specialised cells use little energy.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग हिस्सों का तय काम और आपसी तालमेल
terms.everyday_image: रसोई की टीम में काम बँटा है, फिर भी खाना साथ मिलकर तैयार होता है

why_chain.step: One cell cannot efficiently perform every task of a large organism.
Sharing work permits specialised groups to coordinate into higher levels.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: heart tissues cooperate to pump blood.
unpack.consequence: Explains the next hierarchy from cells to organism.
unpack.visual_verb: remove extra tasks from one cell and connect cooperating groups
unpack.level_extra: Reduced workload does not mean reduced metabolic activity in every specialised cell.

p001-i8.content: Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms. The arrows connect progressively larger levels of biological organisation; they do not represent stages of one cell turning directly into an organism.
p001-i8.exam_note: Know the correct order and distinguish adjacent levels.

p001-i9.content: Cell: first level; arrow points to Tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the starting unit in this hierarchy?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cell is the starting level shown before tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does a cell fit in the organisation of a body?
teacher_understanding.answer: It forms part of a tissue rather than being an organ by itself.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the first arrow work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells associate and cooperate to form a functional tissue group.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की सबसे छोटी जीवित काम करने वाली इकाई
terms.everyday_image: दीवार में एक ईंट, पर cell खुद जीवित है

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: one muscle cell within muscle tissue.
unpack.consequence: Many cooperating cells form the next level.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom from one cell to a group
unpack.level_extra: The hierarchy is organisational, not a cell-division sequence.

p001-i10.content: Tissues: between Cell and Organ; arrow points to Organ.

teacher_understanding.question: What level links cells with organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tissues are the intermediate level displayed.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are tissues found relative to organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different tissues are constituent parts of an organ.

teacher_understanding.question: How can tissues together perform an organ's job?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each contributes a different function, such as contraction, support or signalling, to the organ's combined activity.

p001-i10.exam_note: Do not equate tissue with organ.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: several tissues contribute to the heart.
unpack.consequence: Tissue cooperation creates the organ level.
unpack.visual_verb: assemble different tissue groups
unpack.level_extra: An organ ordinarily contains more than one tissue type.

p001-i11.content: Organ: between Tissues and Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: What is an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: An organ is a body part in which different tissues cooperate in particular functions.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does Organ sit in this flow?
teacher_understanding.answer: It follows Tissues and precedes Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: How does an organ differ from a tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: A tissue is a functional group of cells; an organ combines different tissues into a larger working part.

terms.plain_meaning: कई tissues से बना शरीर का काम करने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: heart में अलग हिस्से मिलकर खून पंप करते हैं

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: heart in animals; leaf in plants.
unpack.consequence: Organs coordinate in organ systems.
unpack.visual_verb: outline an organ around its tissues
unpack.level_extra: Leaf is an organ, not a tissue.

p001-i12.content: Organ system: between Organ and Organisms.

teacher_understanding.question: What is an organ system?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a set of organs cooperating in a major body function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is it placed in the printed hierarchy?
teacher_understanding.answer: Above an organ and below the complete organism.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are several organs needed for a major function?
teacher_understanding.answer: A task such as digestion involves several linked jobs, so different organs perform connected parts of the process.

terms.plain_meaning: एक बड़ा काम मिलकर करने वाले organs की टीम
terms.everyday_image: खाना सँभालने में मुँह, पेट और आँत की जुड़ी हुई टीम

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: digestive system.
unpack.consequence: Systems cooperate within the whole organism.
unpack.visual_verb: connect organs into a working route
unpack.level_extra: A system is not merely a larger single organ.

p001-i13.content: Organisms: final level, receiving the arrow from Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the final label represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: The complete living individual, rather than one of its component systems.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the organism appear in the sequence?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the final level after Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the lower levels contribute to a whole organism?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells, tissues, organs and systems carry out interdependent functions that sustain the individual.

p001-i13.exam_note: The printed plural names a level, not an ecological population.

terms.plain_meaning: पूरा जीवित व्यक्ति, पौधा या जानवर
terms.everyday_image: पूरा आम का पेड़, सिर्फ उसकी एक पत्ती नहीं

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a human being.
unpack.consequence: Completes the organisational hierarchy.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom out to the complete individual
unpack.level_extra: This multicellular hierarchy does not mean every organism has tissues and organs.

p001-i14.content: Comparison table with columns Mitosis and Meiosis and 11 numbered rows.
p001-i14.exam_note: Several standard statement-combination contrasts; row 9 is scientifically unreliable as printed.

p001-i15.content: 1) Mitosis: It occurs in somatic cells. | Meiosis: It occurs in germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cell categories are contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis is associated with somatic cells, whereas meiosis is associated with germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between somatic and germ cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic cells belong to the body-cell category; germ-line cells belong to the reproductive lineage that can produce gametes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is meiosis linked with the reproductive lineage?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sexual reproduction requires chromosome reduction before fusion of gametes; ordinary body growth requires preservation of the chromosome set.

p001-i15.exam_note: Germ cells and mature gametes are not interchangeable terms; germ-line cells can also undergo mitosis.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर के सामान्य हिस्से बनाने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: त्वचा में घाव भरने वाले cells

terms.plain_meaning: gametes बनाने वाली वंश-रेखा के cells
terms.everyday_image: अगली पीढ़ी तक जानकारी पहुँचाने वाली तैयारी की लाइन

why_chain.step: Body maintenance and sexual reproduction have different chromosome requirements.
Mitosis maintains sets; meiosis reduces them in reproductive development.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: skin cell renewal versus sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Explains the different functions listed in row 6.
unpack.visual_verb: split a body-maintenance route from a reproductive route
unpack.level_extra: Avoid turning the row into an absolute claim that germ-line cells never divide mitotically.

p001-i16.content: 2) Mitosis: Nucleus divides only once. | Meiosis: Nucleus divides twice.

teacher_understanding.question: How many nuclear divisions does each process involve?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis involves one, while meiosis involves two.

teacher_understanding.question: What differs between the two meiotic divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are two divisions needed after one DNA replication?
teacher_understanding.answer: The first reduces the chromosome sets and the second distributes the copied chromatids, producing haploid products.

p001-i16.exam_note: Two meiotic divisions do not mean two rounds of DNA replication.

terms.plain_meaning: cell का वह हिस्सा जहाँ chromosomes रखे होते हैं
terms.everyday_image: जरूरी निर्देशों की फाइल रखने वाला कमरा

why_chain.step: Reproductive cells need reduced chromosome sets.
Meiosis separates chromosome pairs first and copied halves next.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: formation of reproductive cells.
unpack.consequence: Leads to two versus four daughter cells.
unpack.visual_verb: show one split beside two successive splits
unpack.level_extra: Remember one replication followed by two meiotic divisions.

p001-i17.content: 3) Mitosis: Two daughter cells are formed. | Meiosis: Four daughter cells are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: What daughter-cell counts are printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Two for mitosis and four for meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these numbers reflect the division pattern?
teacher_understanding.answer: One completed division produces two products; two successive divisions can produce four.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the four-product statement be interpreted in egg formation?
teacher_understanding.answer: In animal oogenesis the divisions are unequal, producing an ovum and polar bodies rather than four equivalent functional eggs.

p001-i17.exam_note: Do not equate four meiotic products with four functional gametes in every case.

terms.plain_meaning: एक cell के बँटने से बने नए cells
terms.everyday_image: एक से दो और फिर दो से चार हिस्सों का पेड़

why_chain.step: Genetic material must be distributed into new cells.
One division yields two products; a second division gives the usual four-product pattern.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: four meiotic products in sperm development.
unpack.consequence: Cell count and chromosome-set count must be tracked separately.
unpack.visual_verb: branch one-to-two and one-to-two-to-four
unpack.level_extra: Oogenesis is the standard qualification.

p001-i18.content: 4) Mitosis: Daughter cells are diploid. | Meiosis: Daughter cells are haploid.

teacher_understanding.question: Which chromosome-set states are contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table contrasts diploid mitotic daughters with haploid meiotic daughters.

teacher_understanding.question: What do diploid and haploid mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: Diploid means two chromosome sets, represented by 2n; haploid means one set, represented by n. Here n counts a set, not DNA mass.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must the mitosis statement be qualified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis generally preserves the parent's chromosome-set number: a haploid parent can also divide mitotically. Diploid daughters describe the usual diploid-parent example.

p001-i18.exam_note: Mitosis preserves ploidy; it does not inherently create diploidy.

terms.plain_meaning: chromosomes के दो पूरे sets वाला
terms.everyday_image: निर्देशों की दो पूरी किताबें

terms.plain_meaning: chromosomes का एक पूरा set वाला
terms.everyday_image: निर्देशों की एक पूरी किताब

why_chain.step: Gamete fusion combines chromosome sets.
Meiosis reduces sets beforehand, preventing doubling across generations.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: human body cells and gametes illustrate the usual diploid–haploid contrast.
unpack.consequence: Connects to reduction division in row 11.
unpack.visual_verb: reduce two colour-coded sets to one
unpack.level_extra: Ploidy is not the same as DNA quantity.

p001-i19.content: 5) Mitosis: It occurs more frequently. | Meiosis: It occurs less frequently.

teacher_understanding.question: What frequency contrast does the table give?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes mitosis as more frequent and meiosis as less frequent.

teacher_understanding.question: What functional difference makes this a reasonable broad contrast?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis supports growth and renewal in many tissues, while meiosis is restricted to particular reproductive stages and lineages.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should this not be treated as a measured universal rule?
teacher_understanding.answer: Actual division frequency depends on the organism, tissue and life stage; the page supplies no counting interval or quantitative evidence.

p001-i19.exam_note: A qualitative generalisation, not a fixed numerical ratio.

why_chain.step: Growth and tissue renewal recur throughout many parts of a body.
Mitosis therefore has a broader routine role than reproductive meiosis.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: repeated skin renewal.
unpack.consequence: Links frequency to function rather than speed of an individual division.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight many renewal sites and a restricted reproductive site
unpack.level_extra: More frequent does not necessarily mean each division takes less time.

p001-i20.content: 6) Mitosis: Daughter cells form somatic organs. | Meiosis: Daughter cells form gametes.

teacher_understanding.question: What destinations are assigned to daughter cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table links mitotic daughters with somatic organs and meiotic daughters with gametes.

teacher_understanding.question: How does body building differ from gamete production?
teacher_understanding.answer: Body building increases or replaces cells in the individual; gametes participate in sexual reproduction by fusion.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the gamete statement need qualification in plants?
teacher_understanding.answer: In flowering plants meiosis produces spores; gametes develop later through the gametophyte stage. The table's wording fits the usual animal summary more directly.

p001-i20.exam_note: Plant meiosis produces spores, not directly gametes in the standard flowering-plant life cycle.

terms.plain_meaning: मिलकर नया जीव शुरू करने वाले reproductive cells
terms.everyday_image: sperm और egg का मिलना

why_chain.step: Growth maintains an individual; sexual reproduction starts a new one.
These needs explain the table's body-cell versus gamete contrast.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: wound repair and sperm production.
unpack.consequence: Connects division type with biological purpose.
unpack.visual_verb: route daughters toward repair or reproduction
unpack.level_extra: Do not apply the animal shortcut uncritically to plant life cycles.

p001-i21.content: 7) Mitosis: There is only one prophase, one metaphase one anaphase and one telophase. | Meiosis: There are two of each phase and five sub-phases in prophase - 1.

teacher_understanding.question: How are the phase sequences compared?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis has one sequence of prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase; meiosis has two sequences, with five subdivisions of prophase I.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes prophase I especially distinctive?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologous chromosomes pair and crossing over can occur, unlike the ordinary mitotic sequence.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are there two versions of each phase in meiosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: The phases belong to two successive nuclear divisions, meiosis I and meiosis II.

p001-i21.exam_note: Prophase I, not prophase II, has the five standard subdivisions.

terms.plain_meaning: meiosis की पहली division का शुरू वाला चरण
terms.everyday_image: बँटवारे से पहले जोड़ों को पास लाकर तैयारी करना

why_chain.step: Meiosis must organise homologous pairs before separating them.
Its first prophase includes pairing and exchange, making it more elaborate.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside addition: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis are the five prophase-I subdivisions.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the crossing-over comparison.
unpack.visual_verb: repeat a four-stage strip and expand prophase I
unpack.level_extra: Crossing over is conventionally associated with pachytene.

p001-i22.content: 8) Mitosis: Number of chromosomes are not changed in the daughter cells. | Meiosis: Number of chromosomes are reduced to half.

teacher_understanding.question: How does daughter chromosome number compare with the parent?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is maintained in mitosis and reduced to half in meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What separates in the reduction step?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I, reducing two sets to one.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is chromosome reduction useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: It allows gamete fusion to restore the diploid condition without doubling chromosome sets in each generation.

p001-i22.exam_note: Chromosome reduction occurs in meiosis I.

why_chain.step: Fusion combines the chromosome contributions of two gametes.
Halving beforehand maintains the usual set number across generations.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: reproductive cell formation before fertilisation.
unpack.consequence: Explains equational versus reduction division.
unpack.visual_verb: compare unchanged sets with halved sets
unpack.level_extra: Count chromosome sets separately from copied DNA.

p001-i23.content: 9) Mitosis: Chromosome number doubles at the beginning of each cell division. | Meiosis: Chromosome number is not doubled. It doubles after the end of first meiotic division. [Scientific correction: DNA replicates before mitosis and before meiosis I; there is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II. DNA replication does not itself double chromosome number.]

teacher_understanding.question: What contrast is actually printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The mitosis column claims chromosome number doubles at the beginning of each division; the meiosis column says it is not doubled and then claims doubling after the first meiotic division.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the correct distinction between DNA replication and chromosome-number change?
teacher_understanding.answer: Replication copies DNA and produces sister chromatids while chromosome number, counted by centromeres, remains unchanged at that stage.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the printed meiotic timing incorrect?
teacher_understanding.answer: DNA is replicated before meiosis I, not after it; there is no intervening replication before meiosis II. This permits reduction rather than restoration of DNA before the second division.

p001-i23.exam_note: Do not memorise this row as a correct statement. Distinguish DNA content, chromosome number and timing of replication.

terms.plain_meaning: chromosomes की गिनती, DNA की कुल मात्रा नहीं
terms.everyday_image: एक फाइल की दूसरी कॉपी जुड़ने से फाइलों की गिनती और पन्नों की मात्रा एक बात नहीं रहती

why_chain.step: Dividing cells need copied genetic instructions.
DNA is copied before mitosis or meiosis I, but not between the two meiotic divisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: the predivision S phase.
unpack.consequence: Prevents the printed error from corrupting the chromosome comparisons.
unpack.visual_verb: copy chromatids while keeping a separate chromosome counter
unpack.level_extra: Treat the bracket as a scientific correction, not as words printed in the source.

p001-i24.content: 10) Mitosis: No crossing over in chromosomes. | Meiosis: Crossing over occurs chromosomes [occurs in chromosomes].

teacher_understanding.question: How does the table contrast crossing over?
teacher_understanding.answer: It presents crossing over as absent in mitosis and present in meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What is exchanged during meiotic crossing over?
teacher_understanding.answer: Corresponding DNA segments are exchanged between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this contribute to variation?
teacher_understanding.answer: It creates new combinations of inherited variants on chromosomes, making gametes genetically different.

p001-i24.exam_note: Standard association: crossing over in prophase I; avoid confusing homologous chromosomes with sister chromatids.

terms.plain_meaning: मिलते-जुलते chromosome जोड़े के बीच DNA के हिस्सों की अदला-बदली
terms.everyday_image: दो रंग की डोरियों में बराबर जगह के छोटे टुकड़े बदलना

why_chain.step: Sexual reproduction produces varied genetic combinations.
Exchange between homologous chromosomes reshuffles inherited combinations.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: prophase I in reproductive cell development.
unpack.consequence: Meiosis introduces variation as well as chromosome reduction.
unpack.visual_verb: exchange matching coloured chromosome segments
unpack.level_extra: The table describes the standard mitosis–meiosis contrast; rare mitotic recombination is not its focus.

p001-i25.content: 11) Mitosis: Equation division [Equational division]. | Meiosis: Reduction division.

teacher_understanding.question: What names summarise the chromosome outcomes?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table calls mitosis equational division and meiosis reduction division.

teacher_understanding.question: What is equal or reduced in these terms?
teacher_understanding.answer: Equational refers to preserving chromosome-set number; reduction refers to halving it, not to reducing cell size.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should the two meiotic divisions be distinguished?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meiosis I is reductional because homologues separate; meiosis II is equational because sister chromatids separate without another reduction in set number.

p001-i25.exam_note: Meiosis as a whole is reductional; meiosis II is equational.

terms.plain_meaning: जिस division में chromosome sets की गिनती बनी रहती है
terms.everyday_image: दो नए पैकेट, दोनों में निर्देशों का वही पूरा set

terms.plain_meaning: जिस division में chromosome sets आधे हो जाते हैं
terms.everyday_image: दो पूरे sets में से हर नए पैकेट को एक set मिलना

why_chain.step: Body renewal needs chromosome continuity, whereas sexual reproduction needs reduction.
The two names summarise these different chromosome outcomes.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: skin renewal and meiosis I.
unpack.consequence: Summarises rows 4 and 8.
unpack.visual_verb: stamp unchanged versus halved on chromosome sets
unpack.level_extra: Equational does not mean equal cell size.

p001-i26.content: Table 7.3: Difference between mitosis in Plants and Animals. Columns: Plants | Animals. Four comparison rows.
p001-i26.exam_note: Typical plant–animal mitosis and cytokinesis distinctions.

p001-i27.content: Plants: Centrioles are absent. | Animals: Centrioles are present.

teacher_understanding.question: What centriole contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The plant column states absence and the animal column presence.

teacher_understanding.question: Does absence of centrioles mean plants lack a spindle?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Typical higher-plant cells organise spindle microtubules without the animal-style centriole-containing centrosome.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this distinction be applied?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use it as a typical higher-plant versus animal-cell comparison, not an exception-free statement about every plant group or animal cell.

p001-i27.exam_note: Centriole absence is not spindle absence.

terms.plain_meaning: animal cell के division organising हिस्से में मिलने वाली छोटी बेलन जैसी बनावटें
terms.everyday_image: दो छोटी पाइप जैसी बनावटें साथ रखी हों

why_chain.step: Chromosomes need a spindle to separate.
Plants can organise this spindle without typical centrioles.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: dividing cells of an onion root tip.
unpack.consequence: Connects to the aster comparison.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast spindle poles with and without centrioles
unpack.level_extra: Typical school-level comparison; retain biological qualifications.

p001-i28.content: Plants: Asters are not formed. | Animals: Asters are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: How is aster formation contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table shows no asters in plants and asters in animals.

teacher_understanding.question: What is an aster rather than the whole spindle?
teacher_understanding.answer: An aster is a star-like array of microtubules radiating around an animal spindle pole; it is not the complete spindle between the poles.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does this follow the centriole comparison?
teacher_understanding.answer: Typical animal centrosomes organise conspicuous radial arrays, while typical higher-plant mitotic cells lack that astral arrangement.

p001-i28.exam_note: Asters absent does not mean chromosome-moving fibres absent.

terms.plain_meaning: division के सिरे के आसपास तारे की किरणों जैसी फैली fibres
terms.everyday_image: बीच से चारों ओर निकली सूरज की किरणें

why_chain.step: Division fibres need organisation around spindle poles.
Typical animal poles show radial asters; typical plant poles do not.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a typical dividing animal cell.
unpack.consequence: Adds a visible feature to the centriole contrast.
unpack.visual_verb: radiate short fibres around animal poles
unpack.level_extra: Keep aster and spindle distinct.

p001-i29.content: Plants: Cell division involves formation of a cell plate. | Animals: Cell division involves furrowing and cleavage of cytoplasm.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the two cells partition cytoplasm?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant cells form a cell plate; animal cells divide through furrowing and cleavage of cytoplasm.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the directions of partitioning differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: The plant cell plate develops centrally and extends outward; the animal cleavage furrow constricts inward from the surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant use a plate rather than the same pinching mechanism?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its rigid cell wall prevents the animal-style constriction, so a new partition is built between the daughter regions.

p001-i29.exam_note: This is cytokinesis, not the chromosome-separation event itself.

terms.plain_meaning: दो नए plant cells के बीच अंदर से बनने वाली नई partition
terms.everyday_image: कमरे के बीच नई दीवार खड़ी करना

terms.plain_meaning: बाहर से बीच की तरफ खाँच बनाकर सिकुड़ना
terms.everyday_image: नरम थैली को बीच में डोरी से कसना

why_chain.step: After nuclear separation, daughter regions need separate cytoplasm.
A rigid plant wall favours building a partition, while animal cells can pinch inward.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside comparison: onion root-tip cells and animal tissue cells.
unpack.consequence: Explains a structural reason for different division appearances.
unpack.visual_verb: build outward versus pinch inward
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse cell plate with metaphase plate.

p001-i30.content: Plants: Occurs mainly at meristem. | Animals: Occurs in tissues throughout the body.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the distribution of mitosis differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is described as mainly meristematic in plants and distributed among tissues throughout animal bodies.

teacher_understanding.question: What does localised plant growth contrast with in animals?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plants concentrate much growth in dividing regions, whereas animal cell renewal occurs at many tissue sites.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must 'throughout the body' not mean every animal cell divides?
teacher_understanding.answer: Division capacity differs among tissues; some specialised cells, such as mature neurons, ordinarily do not divide.

p001-i30.exam_note: Mainly is important: plant mitosis is not an absolute meristem-only rule.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे का वह बढ़ने वाला हिस्सा जहाँ cells लगातार बँटते हैं
terms.everyday_image: जड़ या टहनी की बढ़ती नोक

why_chain.step: A plant needs new cells at growing regions.
Meristems supply much of this new growth through division.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: root tip versus renewal in skin and intestine.
unpack.consequence: Provides the bridge to the plant-tissue chart.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight plant tips and several animal renewal sites
unpack.level_extra: Location statements are common correct-statement traps.

p001-i31.content: Classification of Plant Tissue. Plant Tissue branches into Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue. Meristematic Tissue branches into Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem. Permanent Tissue branches into Simple and Complex. Simple branches into Paranchyma [Parenchyma], Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma. Sclerenchyma branches into Fibres and Sclereids. Complex branches into Xylem and Phloem. Visible Xylem components: Tracheids, Vessels (Tracheae), Xylem parenchyma. Visible Phloem components: Sieve tubes, Companion cells, Phloem parenchyma. The component boxes are cropped at the bottom.
p001-i31.exam_note: Learn complete visible parent–child relationships; do not treat all labels as equal-level categories.

p001-i32.content: Classification of Plant Tissue: root heading branching to Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two main tissue groups open the chart?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue are the first two branches.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes these groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic cells retain active division capacity; permanent tissues are differentiated for particular functions and generally no longer divide actively.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the distinction matter to plant growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: The plant needs a continuing source of new cells as well as specialised cells that carry out established functions.

p001-i32.exam_note: The first classification is not simple versus complex.

why_chain.step: Plants need both new cells and specialised working tissues.
The primary division separates growth-producing from differentiated tissue groups.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside contrast: growing root tip and mature stem tissues.
unpack.consequence: Sets the parent categories for every lower branch.
unpack.visual_verb: split the root into two main branches
unpack.level_extra: Use a parent–child map for odd-one-out questions.

p001-i33.content: Meristematic Tissue: child of Plant Tissue; parent of Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meristem types are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical, lateral and intercalary meristems.

teacher_understanding.question: On what basis do these three differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: They differ primarily by position in the plant and the growth their positions support.

teacher_understanding.question: How does meristematic tissue support growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its dividing cells produce additional cells, some of which later differentiate into permanent tissues.

p001-i33.exam_note: Memorise all three types with locations.

terms.plain_meaning: नए cells बनाकर पौधे को बढ़ाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: इमारत में नई ईंटें जोड़ती काम करती टीम

why_chain.step: A growing plant needs a continuing supply of cells.
Meristematic cells divide and provide that supply.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: the tip of a growing root.
unpack.consequence: Position produces three named meristem categories.
unpack.visual_verb: multiply cells at growth zones
unpack.level_extra: Meristematic tissue is not a subtype of permanent tissue.

p001-i34.content: Apical Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent category contains apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It belongs to Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How is it distinguished from lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristem is at root and shoot tips and mainly supports length growth, whereas lateral meristem supports thickening.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a tip location useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: New cells near the growing end enable a root or shoot to extend into new space.

p001-i34.exam_note: Apical means tip; associate with primary length growth.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ और shoot की नोक पर नए cells बनाने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: नई टहनी की बढ़ती हुई नोक

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots need to extend.
Cell production at their tips supplies length growth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a germinating seed's root tip.
unpack.consequence: Distinguishes length growth from lateral thickening.
unpack.visual_verb: extend the root and shoot tips
unpack.level_extra: Match position, name and growth outcome.

p001-i35.content: Lateral Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue group includes lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic Tissue includes it.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its growth role differ from an apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems increase girth rather than primarily extending the tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a lateral meristem thicken a stem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dividing layers along the sides produce additional tissues, increasing diameter.

p001-i35.exam_note: Lateral meristem–girth is a common matching pair.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे की बगल की दिशा में मोटाई बढ़ाने वाले cells का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: पेड़ का तना सालों में मोटा होना

why_chain.step: A larger plant needs greater thickness and supporting tissue.
Lateral dividing layers add tissue and increase girth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular cambium in a woody stem.
unpack.consequence: Separates secondary thickening from tip extension.
unpack.visual_verb: expand concentric stem layers
unpack.level_extra: Cambium is a standard example; not all plants show substantial secondary growth.

p001-i36.content: Intercalary Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains intercalary meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is one of the three Meristematic Tissue branches.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its position differ from an apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs between mature tissue regions, commonly at leaf bases or internode bases in grasses, rather than only at the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this help a grazed grass plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Growth near the base can remain active after upper parts are removed, enabling regrowth.

terms.plain_meaning: बड़े हो चुके हिस्सों के बीच बचा हुआ बढ़ने वाला भाग
terms.everyday_image: ऊपर से कटी घास का नीचे से फिर बढ़ना

why_chain.step: Grass can lose its exposed upper parts.
Basal dividing regions can continue supplying new growth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a lawn after mowing.
unpack.consequence: Completes the positional meristem classification.
unpack.visual_verb: regrow a cut grass blade from its base
unpack.level_extra: Intercalary does not mean a lateral thickening layer.

p001-i37.content: Permanent Tissue: child of Plant Tissue; parent of Simple and Complex.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two permanent-tissue branches are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple and Complex.

teacher_understanding.question: How does permanent tissue differ from meristematic tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Permanent tissues have differentiated for particular jobs and generally lack the active division characteristic of meristems.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are differentiated tissues necessary?
teacher_understanding.answer: Newly produced cells must acquire features suited to storage, support or transport rather than remaining only a dividing population.

p001-i37.exam_note: Permanent does not mean all its cells are dead.

terms.plain_meaning: खास काम के लिए तैयार हो चुका tissue
terms.everyday_image: सीखने के बाद तय काम सँभालती टीम

why_chain.step: Plants need working cells, not only growing cells.
Differentiation produces tissues specialised for established functions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: storage tissue in a potato.
unpack.consequence: Branches by whether the tissue has one main cell type or multiple cooperating types.
unpack.visual_verb: transform new cells into specialised workers
unpack.level_extra: Some living permanent cells can regain division capacity under appropriate conditions.

p001-i38.content: Simple: child of Permanent Tissue; parent of Paranchyma [Parenchyma], Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three simple permanent tissues are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does simple differ from complex permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple tissue consists mainly of one kind of cell; complex tissue combines different kinds working together.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is simple not a measure of usefulness?
teacher_understanding.answer: The term describes cellular composition, not the importance or difficulty of the tissue's job.

p001-i38.exam_note: Xylem and phloem are not simple tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्यतः एक तरह के cells से बना tissue
terms.everyday_image: एक जैसे काम करने वाले लोगों की टीम

why_chain.step: Tissues can be grouped by their cell composition.
One main cell type defines the simple category.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: parenchyma in fleshy plant parts.
unpack.consequence: Provides the parent for three commonly tested names.
unpack.visual_verb: group three leaves beneath one branch
unpack.level_extra: Simple refers to composition, not absence of specialisation.

p001-i39.content: Complex: child of Permanent Tissue; parent of Xylem and Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissues are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem and Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How are complex tissues unlike simple tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several cell types cooperate within a complex tissue rather than one main type forming the tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is more than one cell type useful in transport tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Conduction, maintenance, storage and support require complementary cellular features.

p001-i39.exam_note: Both conducting tissues belong to complex permanent tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: कई तरह के cells मिलकर एक बड़ा काम करें
terms.everyday_image: पानी की व्यवस्था में पाइप, सहारा और देखरेख की अलग भूमिकाएँ

why_chain.step: Plant transport needs several coordinated jobs.
Different cell types cooperate as complex tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular bundles in a stem.
unpack.consequence: Explains why the xylem and phloem boxes list components.
unpack.visual_verb: combine different cell shapes into one transport bundle
unpack.level_extra: Complex tissue is not an organ.

p001-i40.content: Paranchyma [Parenchyma]: child of Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is parenchyma classified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Under Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How is it broadly unlike sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma generally has living, relatively thin-walled cells; mature sclerenchyma commonly has thick lignified walls and dead cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How do its features suit storage?
teacher_understanding.answer: Living cells with space for stored materials can retain food or water in fleshy plant parts.

p001-i40.exam_note: Printed spelling is incorrect; standard term is Parenchyma.

terms.plain_meaning: अक्सर पतली दीवार वाले जीवित cells का सामान्य plant tissue
terms.everyday_image: आलू का मुलायम अंदरूनी भाग

why_chain.step: Plants need places to store food and water.
Living parenchyma cells can perform these storage roles.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: potato storage tissue.
unpack.consequence: Introduces one of the three simple tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: fill thin-walled cells with stored material
unpack.level_extra: Parenchyma can have other functions; storage is not its only role.

p001-i41.content: Collenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent category contains collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does collenchyma differ from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collenchyma provides flexible support through living cells with uneven wall thickening, unlike the usually rigid, lignified mature sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Young plant parts must resist bending while still growing and moving in the wind.

p001-i41.exam_note: Flexible support and uneven wall thickening distinguish it.

terms.plain_meaning: बढ़ते plant हिस्सों को लचीला सहारा देने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: नरम डंठल मुड़ता है पर तुरंत टूटता नहीं

why_chain.step: Young stems need support without becoming rigid.
Unevenly thickened living cells provide flexible reinforcement.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: beneath the surface of many young dicot stems and in leaf stalks.
unpack.consequence: Contrasts with the harder support of sclerenchyma.
unpack.visual_verb: bend a supported young stalk
unpack.level_extra: Do not assign lignified dead-cell features to collenchyma.

p001-i42.content: Sclerenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue; parent of Fibres and Sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two sclerenchyma forms are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres and Sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: How does sclerenchyma differ from collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mature sclerenchyma commonly provides rigid support through thick lignified walls and cells that are dead at maturity; collenchyma is living and flexible.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can dead cells still support a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mechanical strength resides in their persistent thick walls, so continued living contents are not required for that support.

p001-i42.exam_note: Fibres and sclereids are subtypes, not peers of sclerenchyma.

terms.plain_meaning: मोटी कड़ी दीवार वाले cells से बना मजबूत सहारा देने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: नारियल का कड़ा और रेशेदार हिस्सा

why_chain.step: Mature plant parts need strength and protection.
Thick lignified walls provide durable mechanical support.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: coconut husk fibres.
unpack.consequence: Branches into long fibres and varied sclereids.
unpack.visual_verb: thicken and harden cell walls
unpack.level_extra: Cell death does not imply loss of structural function.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains the Fibres branch?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibres differ from typical sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres are long, narrow cells, whereas sclereids are generally shorter or irregularly shaped.

teacher_understanding.question: How does an elongated form help support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long thick-walled cells can form reinforcing strands that resist pulling forces.

p001-i43.exam_note: Match long narrow form with fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे पतले मजबूत सहारा देने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: नारियल के छिलके से निकलते लंबे रेशे

why_chain.step: Plant parts need resistance to pulling and bending.
Bundles of elongated thick-walled fibres provide reinforcement.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: coconut husk.
unpack.consequence: One of two sclerenchyma forms.
unpack.visual_verb: bundle long reinforcing cells
unpack.level_extra: The chart's generic fibres label is not itself a separate complex tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent contains sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How are sclereids unlike typical fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are generally shorter and occur in varied shapes rather than being uniformly long and narrow.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can they make a plant part feel gritty or hard?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their thick lignified walls form hard inclusions or protective tissue.

p001-i44.exam_note: Sclereids are often called stone cells.

terms.plain_meaning: मोटी कड़ी दीवार वाले छोटे या अलग-अलग आकार के cells
terms.everyday_image: नाशपाती खाते समय महसूस होने वाले कड़क दाने

why_chain.step: Some plant parts need local hardness or protection.
Thick-walled sclereids provide that hardness.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: gritty stone cells in pear flesh.
unpack.consequence: Completes the visible sclerenchyma subdivision.
unpack.visual_verb: scatter hard cells within soft fruit tissue
unpack.level_extra: Use pear grit to distinguish sclereids from long fibres.

p001-i45.where_on_page: chart, lower left component box header
p001-i45.content: Xylem: child of Complex permanent tissue; visible components are Tracheids, Vessels (Tracheae), and Xylem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible components belong to xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids, vessels or tracheae, and xylem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does xylem differ functionally from phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly conducts water and mineral nutrients; phloem transports sugars and other organic solutes.

teacher_understanding.question: How do different xylem cell types cooperate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Conducting elements carry water while living parenchyma contributes storage and lateral movement.

p001-i45.exam_note: Xylem is not wholly dead tissue; its parenchyma is living. The printed box is cropped.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला complex tissue
terms.everyday_image: जड़ से पत्तियों तक पानी की पाइपलाइन

why_chain.step: Leaves need water absorbed by roots.
Xylem provides a conducting pathway with supporting cell types.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular tissue in a stem.
unpack.consequence: Connects the complex category to its component cells.
unpack.visual_verb: move water through a stem bundle
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that the three visible entries exhaust the full xylem component list.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do tracheids differ from vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids are elongated tapered conducting cells with water passing through pits; vessel elements join through perforated end walls into vessels.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a mature dead tracheid conduct water?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its hollow interior and wall pits provide a passage without requiring living contents.

p001-i46.exam_note: A xylem conducting element, not a phloem component.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी ले जाने वाले लंबे सिरों पर पतले xylem cells
terms.everyday_image: पास-पास रखी लंबी नलियाँ जिनकी दीवारों से पानी आगे जाता है

why_chain.step: Water needs a connected path through plant tissue.
Hollow tracheids pass water between neighbouring cells through pits.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: xylem of conifers.
unpack.consequence: One route of xylem water conduction.
unpack.visual_verb: pass water through pits between tapered cells
unpack.level_extra: Tracheids are not animal tracheae.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are Vessels (Tracheae) classified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Under Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How is a vessel unlike one tracheid?
teacher_understanding.answer: A vessel is a conducting tube built from vessel elements joined end to end through perforated end walls.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this arrangement aid transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: End-to-end openings provide a relatively continuous route for water movement.

p001-i47.exam_note: Tracheae here is the plant vessel synonym, not the human windpipe.

terms.plain_meaning: कई cells सिरों से जुड़कर बनी xylem की पानी वाली नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: छोटे पाइपों को जोड़कर लंबी पाइपलाइन बनाना

why_chain.step: Water must move along an extended plant axis.
Joined vessel elements create a continuous conducting route.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vessel-bearing xylem in a flowering plant stem.
unpack.consequence: Contrasts a tube of elements with individual tracheids.
unpack.visual_verb: join open-ended elements into a tube
unpack.level_extra: Keep the botanical use of tracheae separate from animal anatomy.

p001-i48.content: Xylem parenchyma: component listed under Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue includes this parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from mature tracheids and vessel elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem parenchyma is living, unlike those mature conducting elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is living parenchyma useful within xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It can store materials and assist lateral transport, complementing the main water-conducting pathway.

p001-i48.exam_note: Common exception to the oversimplification that all xylem is dead.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem के भीतर मौजूद जीवित parenchyma cells
terms.everyday_image: पाइपलाइन के पास भंडार और देखरेख की जगह

why_chain.step: A transport tissue needs storage and sideways exchange as well as long-distance flow.
Living parenchyma supplies these complementary functions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: living cells within woody xylem.
unpack.consequence: Shows why xylem is complex rather than a single cell type.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight living storage cells beside water conduits
unpack.level_extra: A complex tissue can include both living and dead cell types.

p001-i49.where_on_page: chart, lower right component box header
p001-i49.content: Phloem: child of Complex permanent tissue; visible components are Sieve tubes, Companion cells and Phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which phloem components are visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does phloem transport differ from xylem transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem carries sugars and other organic solutes between sources and sinks; xylem chiefly carries water and mineral nutrients.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need a food-distribution tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots, developing fruits and other non-photosynthesising or growing parts need products made elsewhere, commonly in leaves.

p001-i49.exam_note: Phloem transport is not simply an exclusively downward flow. The box is cropped.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बनी sugars और दूसरे organic पदार्थ पहुँचाने वाला complex tissue
terms.everyday_image: रसोई से अलग कमरों तक खाना पहुँचाने की व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Not every plant part makes enough food for itself.
Phloem distributes organic nutrients from sources to consuming or storing parts.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: sugar movement from leaves to a developing fruit.
unpack.consequence: Explains the cooperating phloem components.
unpack.visual_verb: move sugar from leaf to fruit and root
unpack.level_extra: The visible list is not evidence that no other phloem components exist.

p001-i50.content: Sieve tubes: component listed under Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains sieve tubes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do sieve tubes differ from xylem vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve tubes are formed from living conducting elements with sieve plates and carry organic solutes, whereas mature vessel elements are dead water-conducting cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the sieve arrangement allow transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pores in the end-wall sieve plates connect neighbouring elements, permitting phloem sap movement.

p001-i50.exam_note: Sieve-tube elements are living but lack a nucleus at maturity in flowering plants.

terms.plain_meaning: sugars ले जाने वाले जुड़े हुए phloem cells की नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: जोड़ों पर छलनी जैसे छेद वाली पाइप

why_chain.step: Organic nutrients need a connected conducting path.
Sieve plates connect living tube elements for sap transport.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: phloem in a flowering plant stem.
unpack.consequence: Their specialisation explains the need for companion cells.
unpack.visual_verb: pass sap through perforated sieve plates
unpack.level_extra: Lack of a nucleus does not make a mature sieve-tube element dead.

p001-i51.content: Companion cells: component listed under Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue includes companion cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do companion cells differ from mature sieve-tube elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Companion cells retain a nucleus and metabolically support the associated sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this support needed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve-tube elements are specialised for conduction and have reduced internal machinery, so associated companion cells help maintain their functioning.

p001-i51.exam_note: Companion cells associate with sieve tubes, not xylem vessels.

terms.plain_meaning: sieve tubes के साथ रहकर उनका काम सँभालने में मदद करने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य रास्ते के पास उसकी देखभाल करती टीम

why_chain.step: Highly specialised sieve elements have reduced internal machinery.
Nucleated companion cells provide metabolic assistance.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: beside sieve-tube elements in flowering-plant phloem.
unpack.consequence: Demonstrates cooperation within a complex tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: pair a nucleated helper cell with a sieve element
unpack.level_extra: The helper analogy explains cooperation, not a separate organism living in the plant.

p001-i52.content: Phloem parenchyma: component listed under Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains phloem parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How is its role different from that of sieve tubes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem parenchyma mainly contributes living storage and local exchange functions, while sieve tubes form the main long-distance conducting route.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it help explain the word complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: It adds another specialised cell type cooperating with conducting and companion cells in the same tissue.

p001-i52.exam_note: Parenchyma occurs as a component in both visible complex-tissue boxes.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem के जीवित parenchyma cells जो भंडारण जैसे काम करते हैं
terms.everyday_image: खाना पहुँचाने की व्यवस्था के साथ जुड़ा छोटा भंडार

why_chain.step: Food distribution needs storage and local exchange as well as a main conducting path.
Living parenchyma contributes these complementary tasks.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: phloem of many dicot stems.
unpack.consequence: Completes the visible chart and reinforces complex-tissue composition.
unpack.visual_verb: place storage cells beside the sugar pathway
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse the simple-tissue category parenchyma with its named location inside a complex tissue.

map.chapter_summary: Cells performing the same function form tissues, enabling division of labour and organisation from cells to organisms. The page compares mitosis with meiosis, contrasts plant and animal mitosis, and classifies plant tissues into meristematic and permanent tissues, including their visible subdivisions and transport-tissue components.

concepts.name: Tissue and its plant–animal grouping
concepts.core_explanation: Book: A tissue is formed when cells combine to perform the same function; plant cells form plant tissues and animal cells form animal tissues. The defining idea is coordinated function, while plant versus animal identifies the biological group to which the cells belong.

concepts.name: Division of labour and reduced cellular workload
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Tissue formation causes division of labour, decreases the workload on individual cells and leads to organisation. Outside explanation: Specialised groups share different tasks, so an individual cell need not perform the full range of functions required by a multicellular organism.

concepts.name: Levels of biological organisation
concepts.core_explanation: Book: The arrangement is Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms, placing tissues between cells and organs and organ systems between organs and organisms. Outside explanation: Tissues contribute to organs, and cooperating organs form organ systems; these are nested structural levels, not stages in which one cell directly changes into an organism.

concepts.name: Mitosis versus meiosis: occurrence, products and roles
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Mitosis occurs in somatic cells, forms two diploid daughter cells, occurs more frequently and produces daughter cells that form somatic organs; meiosis occurs in germ cells, forms four haploid daughter cells, occurs less frequently and produces cells associated with gamete formation. Outside qualification: This is the book's simplified comparison; mitosis preserves the starting chromosome-set number rather than necessarily producing diploid cells, and meiotic products do not directly become gametes in every life cycle.

concepts.name: Mitosis versus meiosis: nuclear divisions and phases
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Mitosis has one nuclear division with one prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase; meiosis has two nuclear divisions and two occurrences of these phases. Prophase I of meiosis has five sub-phases, so its distinctive detail belongs to the first meiotic division rather than to both divisions.

concepts.name: Chromosome-number outcomes and crossing over
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Mitosis maintains daughter-cell chromosome number and is equational division; meiosis halves chromosome number and is reduction division, with crossing over contrasted against its absence in mitosis. Outside explanation: Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I, producing reduction, while sister chromatids separate in meiosis II; meiotic crossing over exchanges segments between nonsister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

concepts.name: DNA replication is not chromosome-number doubling
concepts.core_explanation: Book claim, scientifically incorrect: The row says chromosome number doubles at the beginning of mitosis, does not double at the beginning of meiosis and doubles after the first meiotic division. Outside correction, also flagged in the supplied transcription: DNA replicates before mitosis and before meiosis I, with no DNA replication between meiosis I and II. Replication creates sister chromatids and increases DNA content; it does not itself double chromosome number.

concepts.name: Plant versus animal mitosis
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Plant mitosis is described as lacking centrioles and asters, involving cell-plate formation and occurring mainly at meristems; animal mitosis has centrioles and asters, involves furrowing and cleavage of cytoplasm, and occurs in tissues throughout the body. Outside explanation and qualification: A cell plate partitions the plant cell, whereas a cleavage furrow constricts the animal cell; the table presents a standard contrast, not a claim that every plant or animal cell follows it without exception.

concepts.name: Main classification of plant tissues
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Plant tissue branches into Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue. Outside explanation: This distinction separates actively dividing growth tissue from differentiated tissue whose cells generally no longer divide, providing a meaningful basis for the two branches.

concepts.name: Meristematic tissue and its three types
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Meristematic Tissue divides into Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem. Outside explanation: Apical meristems occur at root and shoot tips and support length growth; lateral meristems support increased girth, while intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues, for example at leaf bases or internode bases in grasses.

concepts.name: Permanent tissue: simple and complex
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Permanent Tissue branches into Simple and Complex; Simple leads to parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma, while Complex leads to xylem and phloem. Outside explanation: Simple tissues consist of one principal cell type, whereas complex tissues contain different cell types working together.

concepts.name: Simple permanent tissues and sclerenchyma subdivisions
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Parenchyma, printed as 'Paranchyma', Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma are simple permanent tissues; Fibres and Sclereids are subdivisions of Sclerenchyma, not additional peers of the three simple tissues. Outside explanation: Parenchyma commonly contains living, relatively thin-walled cells; collenchyma provides flexible support through uneven wall thickening, while sclerenchyma provides strength through thick, lignified walls, with fibres generally elongated and sclereids shorter and variable in shape.

concepts.name: Xylem and its visible components
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Xylem belongs to complex permanent tissue, and its visible component list contains Tracheids, Vessels (Tracheae) and Xylem parenchyma; cropping prevents treating this list as complete. Outside explanation: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals; tracheids and vessels are conducting elements, whereas xylem parenchyma consists of living cells contributing to storage and lateral transport.

concepts.name: Phloem and its visible components
concepts.core_explanation: Book: Phloem belongs to complex permanent tissue, and the visible components are Sieve tubes, Companion cells and Phloem parenchyma; the cropped diagram does not establish an exhaustive list. Outside explanation: Phloem transports organic food materials; sieve-tube elements conduct them, companion cells support sieve-tube functioning, and phloem parenchyma contributes to storage and lateral movement.

relations.note: Understand a tissue before explaining how tissue specialisation distributes work.
Tissue is one of the nested levels in the organisation diagram.
First establish the two division types and their products, then distinguish their nuclear divisions.
Reduction and equational outcomes require distinguishing meiosis I from meiosis II.
The replication correction refers explicitly to the interval between the two meiotic divisions.
Plant–animal differences are differences within mitosis, not a replacement for the mitosis–meiosis distinction.
The plant-tissue branch of the general tissue grouping is classified further.
Meristematic tissue is one main plant-tissue branch.
Permanent tissue is the other main plant-tissue branch.
Outside explanation: Active division distinguishes meristematic tissue from generally nondividing differentiated permanent tissue.
Mitosis supplies the cell-division context for meristematic growth.
Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma occupy the simple permanent-tissue branch.
Xylem occupies the complex permanent-tissue branch.
Phloem occupies the complex permanent-tissue branch.
Recognising parenchyma helps explain why a complex tissue can contain xylem parenchyma.
Recognising parenchyma helps interpret phloem parenchyma as a component rather than a separate classification branch.
Compare the two complex tissues by their visible component lists; outside explanation adds water/mineral versus organic-food transport.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Cell as a living unit, multicellularity and cell specialisation
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Makes sense of cells sharing functions in tissues and distributing an organism's work.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Cell nucleus, DNA, chromosomes, homologous pairs, sister chromatids and centromeres
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: These are the objects divided, paired or exchanged in the mitosis–meiosis comparison; chromosome counting must be distinguished from DNA quantity.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Chromosome sets: haploid and diploid
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Explains the daughter-cell comparison, chromosome-number maintenance and reduction without relying on memorised labels.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Somatic cells, germ cells, gametes and fertilisation
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Distinguishes the sites and reproductive roles of the two division types and explains why chromosome reduction matters.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Nuclear division, daughter cells, cytokinesis and spindle organisation
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Separates division of the nucleus from division of cytoplasm and gives meaning to phases, centrioles, asters and spindle poles.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Plant and animal cell boundaries, cytoplasm and wall thickening
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Explains cell plate versus cleavage furrow and the thin, unevenly thickened or lignified walls used to clarify simple tissues.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Root and shoot tips, stem girth, leaf bases and internodes
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Provides the spatial vocabulary needed to explain the three meristem names rather than merely recite them.

prerequisites_to_teach.name: Plant water uptake, photosynthetic food production, transport and storage
prerequisites_to_teach.why_needed: Makes the xylem and phloem component groupings understandable through the different materials they handle and the roles of conducting and storage cells.

exam_focus.why: The tissue definition and plant–animal grouping underpin classification questions.
Division of labour is the functional reason for tissue-level organisation.
The cell-to-organism hierarchy supports ordering and incorrectly matched-level questions.
Sites, daughter-cell numbers, chromosome sets and biological roles are high-value comparison criteria.
One versus two nuclear divisions and the five sub-phases of prophase I are distinctive facts.
Equational versus reduction division, chromosome-number outcomes and crossing over are common conceptual discriminators.
The printed error risks incorrect answers; DNA replication must not be confused with chromosome-number doubling.
Centrioles, asters, cytokinesis and division locations form a compact matching and statement-testing set.
The main plant-tissue split anchors the entire classification tree.
The three meristem types are important classification terms; outside location explanations aid discrimination.
Simple versus complex and their immediate descendants are central classification distinctions.
Fibres and sclereids must be placed under sclerenchyma rather than alongside the three simple tissue types.
Xylem component matching, including xylem parenchyma, is useful for classification and odd-one-out questions.
Sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem parenchyma must be distinguished from visible xylem components.
